title: Swapping capslock/ctrl causes ctrl to stick ON (Surface Laptop Studio)

judgment.rationale: The issue reports a persistent stuck-Control symptom on Surface hardware. PR #37930 addressed a related generic stuck-modifier path, but the reporter said the problem persisted on 0.95.1; the existing work is only partial evidence, not a resolution of this report.
evidence: The issue describes Ctrl remaining logically pressed after a CapsLock/Ctrl swap on a Surface Laptop Studio.
PR #37930 merged a generic fix for a related stuck-modifier problem.
The reporter stated the Surface symptom persisted on PowerToys 0.95.1 after that fix.
The thread mentions SharpKeys can show a similar symptom, so the mechanism may not be exclusive to this PowerToys path.
judgment.recommended_action: Retain #37930 as related prior work and re-test the exact Surface sequence on current stable before considering any separate fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: PR #37930 fixed a related generic stuck-modifier issue, but the reporter's v0.95.1 follow-up says this Surface case remained. No competing fix should be designed until the current result and event path are revalidated.

issue_context.summary: A Surface Laptop Studio reporter says Control sticks after a CapsLock/Ctrl remap; a related generic fix did not fully resolve the reported case on the version they tested.
known_information: The report is labeled Issue-Bug, Priority-1, and Product-Keyboard Manager.
PR #37930 merged a generic fix for a related stuck-modifier issue.
The reporter says the symptom remained on PowerToys 0.95.1 after that fix.
A comment reports similar behavior with SharpKeys, which is useful counterevidence against assuming a PowerToys-only cause.
inferences: A modifier key-up or synthetic-event ownership issue remains possible, but the Surface-specific persistence and SharpKeys comparison leave multiple causes open.
The existing PR may have fixed only one manifestation of the broader symptom.
issue_context.analysis: Do not mark this handled based only on #37930. Reproduce with a minimal single mapping on current stable and compare the physical key state and an alternate remapper; only then decide whether a PowerToys-specific change is justified.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue body and all 20 comments, including the report that symptoms persisted on v0.95.1.
Checked PR #37930 as the related merged modifier-state fix; it does not establish that this still-open report is resolved.

actions.label: Re-test the Surface modifier issue after #37930

reproduce.title: Check whether the Surface Ctrl-stuck sequence remains on current stable
prerequisites: Surface Laptop Studio or the reporter's Surface device.
A clean Keyboard Manager profile with only CapsLock mapped to Ctrl.
An alternate remapper only for a controlled comparison, if available.
steps: Confirm Ctrl and CapsLock behave normally with Keyboard Manager disabled.
Enable only the CapsLock-to-Ctrl mapping and repeat the exact sequence described in the issue until the reported stuck state would occur.
If Ctrl sticks, inspect the logical modifier state and record which key-down/up event is missing without capturing typed content.
Compare with the alternate-remapper result and with Keyboard Manager disabled.
reproduce.expected_result: The remapped modifier always returns to an unpressed state after key release, or a focused trace identifies the missing transition beyond the related #37930 fix.
